newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM to discuss action with cenbank on crown.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM to discuss action with cenbank on crown.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Thursday that he would contact central bank Governor Josef Tosovsky soon to discuss what "symbolic" action to take to help the ailing Czech crown.
"I will call the governor of the central bank fast after this interview and we will debate what symbolic action we should do together to support the crown," Klaus said in an interview on Czech Radio.

Klaus said that he believed that the crown should also be helped later on Thursday by a joint statement of the governing coalition on its preparedness to continue in an unaltered course of economic reforms.
The prime minister said the government would hold to its tight fiscal policy, which has helped to cut the differential between budget revenues and expenditures and the overall budget deficit.

He said the crown's sharp fall this morning was a result of the "nervous situation" on the political scene and opposition demands presented in the parliament on Wednesday, which include imposition of import deposits, increased government spending and a slowdown in privatisation and price deregulation.

"I expect to take a number of clear actions. I have also talked about it with Mr. President (Vaclav Havel). I'm persuaded that the coalition leaders who will show readiness to continue further in a unaltered (corrects) economic course will be a stabilising factor," Klaus told the radio.
The leaders of the three-party coalition are supposed to hold talks later today before meeting President Vaclav Havel at 5.30 p.m. (1530 GMT) to debate a planned reshuffle of the government.
Klaus ruled out resignation of the whole cabinet or early elections, saying it would be "impossible, unnecessary and inappropriate".

The crown fell to an all-time low of below minus six percent versus its mark/dollar market on Thursday morning, prompting the central bank to intervene, cut access to Lombard credit and limit non-residents from access to the money market.
At 1115 GMT, the crown was trading at minus 3.52 versus the basket, 30.718 top the dollar and 18.195 to the mark, by 1135 GMT the currency had fallen to below 5.2 percent below parity.
